emulators.name: DuckStation (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: One memory card per game, named as DuckStation names it.

cards.change: Set DuckStation's Memory Card 1 to a separate card per game

emulators.name: PCSX2 (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Shared memory cards by default (Mcd001.ps2, Mcd002.ps2). A game set to its own card in PCSX2's game properties gets <game>.ps2.

emulators.name: Dolphin (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: GameCube saves as files per game (GCI folders, US/EU/JP). Wii saves from its NAND.

emulators.name: PPSSPP (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Each game's save folders, from PPSSPP's SAVEDATA.

emulators.name: RPCS3 (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Each game's save folders, from RPCS3's savedata. RomM's PS3UPDAT.PUP comes down to bios/ps3, to install in RPCS3.

firmware.install: In RPCS3: File, Install Firmware, then pick {file}
firmware.install_without: Add PS3UPDAT.PUP to RomM's PS3 firmware: it comes down to install in RPCS3

emulators.name: Vita3K (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Games come down as RomM has them, to install in Vita3K; ES-DE lists each by a .psvita file. Saves are user 00's, one folder per game. RomM's PSVUPDAT.PUP and PSP2UPDAT.PUP come down to bios/psvita, to install in Vita3K.

firmware.install: In Vita3K: File, Install Firmware, then pick {file} (and the other .pup beside it)
firmware.install_without: In RetroDECK's Configurator: Tools, Install: Vita3K Firmware (or add PSVUPDAT.PUP to RomM's PS Vita firmware)

emulators.name: xemu (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Saves from xemu's hard disk image, wherever xemu.toml puts it.

emulators.name: PrimeHack (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Metroid Prime Trilogy. Wii saves from its NAND, GameCube ones as files per game, kept the way Dolphin keeps them.

emulators.name: MAME (RetroDECK)
emulators.note: Each game's NVRAM, MAME's nvram/<set>/ folder, synced as a zip of it (<set>.zip, its files under <set>/).

emulators.name: Eden
emulators.note: Games with their updates and DLC, keys, firmware and the saves of Eden's current user. Its Flathub Flatpak sees no folder outside its own, so its games go in ~/.var/app/dev.eden_emu.eden/data/eden/games, unless you allow your games folder (flatpak override). The games and updates folders go into Eden's settings while it's closed, once it has started once.

emulators.name: Eden (AppImage)
emulators.note: Games with their updates and DLC, keys, firmware and the saves of Eden's current user, in the folders its settings name (EmuDeck's NAND too). The games and updates folders go into Eden's settings while it's closed, once it has started once.

emulators.name: Citron
emulators.note: Games with their updates and DLC, keys, firmware and the saves of Citron's current user. The games and updates folders go into Citron's settings while it's closed, once it has started once.

emulators.name: Ryujinx
emulators.note: Games with their updates and DLC (Ryujinx's autoload folders), keys, firmware and the saves of Ryujinx's open user. A game's save comes down once Ryujinx has run the game once.

emulators.name: DuckStation
emulators.note: One memory card per game, named as DuckStation names it. Its folders come from DuckStation's settings.ini. Its Flathub Flatpak can't see a games folder outside its own unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/org.duckstation.DuckStation/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

cards.change: Set DuckStation's Memory Card 1 to a separate card per game

emulators.name: PCSX2
emulators.note: Shared memory cards by default (Mcd001.ps2, Mcd002.ps2). A game set to its own card in PCSX2's game properties gets <game>.ps2. Its folders come from PCSX2.ini.

emulators.name: Dolphin
emulators.note: GameCube saves as files per game (GCI folders, USA/EUR/JAP). Wii saves from its NAND, wherever Dolphin.ini puts it.

emulators.name: PrimeHack
emulators.note: Metroid Prime Trilogy. Wii saves from its NAND, and GameCube ones as files per game, kept the way Dolphin keeps them.

emulators.name: PPSSPP
emulators.note: Each game's save folders, from PPSSPP's SAVEDATA.

emulators.name: RPCS3
emulators.note: Each game's save folders, from RPCS3's savedata, wherever vfs.yml puts dev_hdd0. RomM's PS3UPDAT.PUP comes down to install in RPCS3.

firmware.install: In RPCS3: File, Install Firmware, then pick {file}
firmware.install_without: Add PS3UPDAT.PUP to RomM's PS3 firmware: it comes down to install in RPCS3

emulators.name: Xenia
emulators.note: Xbox 360 (Xenia Canary or Edge, the Linux build). Saves sync for the player signed in first, from Xenia's content folder.

emulators.name: Xenia (EmuDeck, Proton)
emulators.note: Xbox 360 (Xenia for Windows, which EmuDeck runs through Proton, portable beside its .exe). Saves sync for the player signed in first, from its content folder.

emulators.name: Vita3K
emulators.note: Games come down as RomM has them, to install in Vita3K; ES-DE lists each by a .psvita file. Saves are those of the user Vita3K signs in (config.yml's user-id), one folder per game, wherever its pref-path is. RomM's PSVUPDAT.PUP and PSP2UPDAT.PUP come down to install in Vita3K.

firmware.install: In Vita3K: File, Install Firmware, then pick {file} (and the other .pup beside it)
firmware.install_without: Add PSVUPDAT.PUP to RomM's PS Vita firmware: it comes down to install in Vita3K

emulators.name: Cemu
emulators.note: Each game's saves from Cemu's mlc01, wherever settings.xml puts it. Games go to Cemu's first game folder.

emulators.name: xemu
emulators.note: Saves from xemu's hard disk image, wherever xemu.toml puts it.

emulators.name: melonDS
emulators.note: Each game's save (.sav), in melonDS's save folder or next to the game. Its Flathub Flatpak sees only your home folder, not the SD card unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/net.kuribo64.melonDS/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

emulators.name: Azahar
emulators.note: Each game's saves from Azahar's SD card folder, wherever qt-config.ini puts it.

emulators.name: Citra / Lime3DS
emulators.note: Azahar's predecessors: each game's saves from the SD card folder, the same as Azahar's.

emulators.name: Flycast
emulators.note: Each game's own memory card syncs as its save (Flycast's default); shared ones are backed up as RomM memory cards. Save states don't sync yet.

cards.change: Turn on Own memory card for each game in its settings (players 2 to 4 always share theirs)

emulators.name: mGBA
emulators.note: Each game's save (.sav), in mGBA's save folder or next to the game.

emulators.name: MAME
emulators.note: Each game's NVRAM, MAME's nvram/<set>/ folder, synced as a zip of it (<set>.zip, its files under <set>/).

emulators.name: ScummVM
emulators.note: Saves by ScummVM's id for the game (its target): <target>.000 or <target>.s00 in its save folder, synced as <target>.zip. The target comes from ES-DE's .scummvm file in the game's folder, else from scummvm.ini's entry for that folder.

emulators.name: RMG (Rosalie's Mupen GUI)
emulators.note: N64 saves: its .eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk files (named by mupen64plus's database) joined into one .srm for RomM, the same as RetroArch's and Mupen64Plus PS5's. Its Flathub Flatpak can't see a games folder outside its own unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/com.github.Rosalie241.RMG/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

emulators.name: simple64
emulators.note: N64 saves: its .eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk files (named by mupen64plus's database) joined into one .srm for RomM, the same as RetroArch's and Mupen64Plus PS5's. Its Flathub Flatpak can't see a games folder outside its own unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/io.github.simple64.simple64/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

emulators.name: gopher64
emulators.note: N64 saves: its <game>-<SHA-256>.eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk files joined into one .srm for RomM, the same as RetroArch's, Mupen64Plus PS5's and RMG's. Its Flathub Flatpak can't see a games folder outside its own unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/io.github.gopher64.gopher64/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

emulators.name: ares
emulators.note: Each game's save files (.ram, and .eeprom, .flash or .rtc where the cartridge has them), beside the game or in ares's Saves folder.

emulators.name: Snes9x
emulators.note: Each game's save (.srm, the same as RetroArch's Snes9x), beside the game or in its SRAM folder. Its Flathub Flatpak sees only your home folder, not the SD card unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/com.snes9x.Snes9x/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

emulators.name: bsnes
emulators.note: Each game's save (.srm, and .rtc for clock carts), beside the game or in its Saves folder.

emulators.name: DeSmuME
emulators.note: Each game's save (.dsv) in DeSmuME's folder: the cartridge save goes to RomM without DeSmuME's footer, shared with melonDS. Its Flathub Flatpak can't see a games folder outside its own unless you allow it (flatpak override): then its games go in ~/.var/app/org.desmume.DeSmuME/data/roms/<system>, where you point it.

emulators.name: Stella
emulators.note: Games only: Atari 2600 cartridges keep no saves.

emulators.name: DOSBox Staging
emulators.note: Games only: a DOS game writes its saves inside its own folder, with no file of its own to sync.

emulators.name: shadPS4
emulators.note: Each game's save folders, shadPS4's savedata/<title id>/ (user 1000's in home/1000/savedata since its user accounts, savedata/1 before), synced as <title id>.zip. The title id comes from the .pkg or the installed game's param.sfo.

emulators.name: Supermodel
emulators.note: Sega Model 3. Each game's NVRAM (<game>.nv). EmuDeck puts a starting one there for every game: it goes to RomM like a save.

emulators.name: Model 2 Emulator
emulators.note: Sega Model 2, EmuDeck's Windows build (Proton). Each game's NVRAM (NVDATA/<game>.DAT); games in roms/model2/roms.

emulators.name: BigPEmu
emulators.note: Atari Jaguar. A cartridge's EEPROM, game<FNV-1a of the game file, in capitals>_eeprom.bigpeep in BigPEmu's UserData. The Jaguar CD's memory track isn't synced.
